mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public or commissioner of oaths in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for non-Canadian issuers) OR Consular Legalization (if origin state is not a Hague Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuer of underlying document (utility provider, bank, or tax authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (where required for foreign-source documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution and certificate of incumbency (where a corporate shareholder is a body corporate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretary of the foreign corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (including certification by the appropriate foreign registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and the opening of a client relationship with the prospective shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution maintaining the shareholder or beneficial owner account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to act as director (Form for Alberta company director) and statutory declaration of capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in Alberta or Canadian consular official
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization; apostille or consular legalization not required for Alberta-executed instruments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the Government of Canada's sanctions lists (Automatic Advanced Passenger Screening, Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) under FINTRAC regulations, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Ongoing monitoring is required at onboarding and on each rescreening cycle of at least every 365 days, or immediately upon any material change or news trigger. FINTRAC reporting obligations apply for suspicious transactions, large cash transactions (threshold CAD 10,000), and terrorism-related financing indicators.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – through the online Alberta Corporate Registry Search and NUANS Name Reservation System; https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French as permitted by the Alberta Business Corporations Act; the name must be clearly distinguishable from existing names or trademarks and must not be misleading. If a foreign-language or transliterated name is used, a certified English or French translation must be submitted as part of the NUANS search package. Numerals and punctuation are permitted subject to the Alberta Name Regulation and corporate name interpretation guidelines.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (where implying educational or professional accreditation)
Architectural or legal designations requiring statutory authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant or incorporator may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations at Service Alberta within 30 days of the rejection date. The appeal must include: (i) the rejected name application reference or NUANS report, (ii) the full proposed name, (iii) a statement of distinctiveness or reasons why the name is not confusingly similar, and (iv) any additional evidence of prior use, trademark registration, or consent from a recognized body. The appeal is submitted through the Alberta Corporate Registry portal or by written correspondence to Service Alberta, Corporate Registry Appeals Division. The Registrar will issue a decision within 30 business days. The appellant may further pursue judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench only after exhausting the administrative appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. The registered office must be a physical street address within Alberta where process may be served during normal business hours. A virtual office or registered agent address is acceptable if the provider maintains a physical Alberta location, accepts service on behalf of the corporation, and offers forwarding of correspondence. A post office box is not sufficient unless used only as an additional mailing address and the physical address requirement is otherwise satisfied.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 2%–5% annual likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection for a standard mobile software application company with no physical retail footprint. The likelihood increases to approximately 10%–15% in the context of FINTRAC compliance audits or law-enforcement inquiries involving beneficial ownership verification. Service Alberta may conduct administrative inspections of registered office compliance, and the Alberta Corporate Registry may require production of corporate records upon request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, as amended; governance and formation provisions (ss. 5-18, 100-112)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, administered through authorized corporate registry service providers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-1 / Alberta Corporate Registry filing instrument)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the ABCA; a corporation may incorporate with nominal share consideration. No escrow account or capital deposit is required. Directors must record the consideration received for issued shares and observe solvency tests in connection with dividends, redemptions, or capital reductions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED:
1. The subscription and issue of the corporation’s authorized common shares are approved; the shares are allotted to the subscriber as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the secretary is instructed to record the allotment and issue share certificates.
2. The address stated in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the corporation’s registered office for service, and a records office is maintained at that address.
3. The following persons are appointed as officers: President, Secretary and Treasurer, together with the sole director named in the consent to act, each to serve until reappointed or replaced.
This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online system through an authorized service provider (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a corporate name search report (NUANS or acceptable Alberta name search) to verify absence of confusingly similar existing corporate names. Submit the desired name for reservation or proceed with a numbered name structure such as "12345678 Alberta Ltd.". The name must be available, not contrary to public policy, and must comply with ABCA naming regulations.
required_dossiers: Name search report
Name reservation request (if a non-numbered name is selected)
Contact details of the incorporating subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the registry will provide the rejection basis. The applicant may submit an alternate name after receiving the written reason or proceed with a numbered Alberta company; application fees are generally non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate registry service provider / registered legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed form, providing corporate name, registered office address in Alberta, authorized share structure, restrictions on share transfers if any, and initial directors. Each initial director must sign a separate Consent to Act as Director.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (INC-1 or authorized service provider equivalent)
Consent to Act as Director for each initial director
Resolution or authorization of the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing package is incomplete or queried, amend the defect and resubmit through the same authorized service provider; a registry requisition will specify the deficiency and must be cured before the certificate issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Service Alberta filing counter or authorized online submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation together with the prescribed incorporation fee and name search charge. Upon acceptance, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which establishes the corporation as a legal entity with limited liability from the date of issuance.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Name search report (if applicable)
Incorporation fee remittance
Authorized service provider or filing form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or refused, the registry will state the specific defect; the applicant may submit corrected Articles or a written response within the requisition period. A refusal does not terminate the application if the deficiency is cured within the specified timeframe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Designate Registered Office and Records Address
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; thereafter the corporation's own registered office address in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the Articles identify a registered office located in Alberta and that the address is a physical street address accessible during normal business hours. At the registered office, the corporation must maintain its minute book, by-laws, share register, directors' register, and other statutory records. If a separate records office is used, file the prescribed notice or maintain the designation in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Registered office street address designation
Consent of the occupant or landlord to use the address
Notice of records office if different from registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the address is invalid or cannot be used, pass a board resolution authorizing a new registered office address and file the appropriate Notice of Change of Registered Office with the Alberta Corporate Registry; late filing risks administrative penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors / corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the statutory first board meeting or execute a written resolution in accordance with ABCA. The first board resolution must approve the share subscription and share issue, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, set the financial year-end, approve the form of share certificate, and establish banking authorities. Maintain the minute book by recording all board resolutions, share certificates, securities register, directors' register, and adopted by-laws.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director
First Board Resolution record or written resolution
Adopted by-laws
Share certificates and securities register
Register of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a step is omitted, the directors may execute a subsequent ratification resolution correcting the record. The correction must be documented in the minute book and any defective share issue should be re-approved and re-issued without retroactive prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Registration and Post-Incorporation Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with CRA to obtain the federal Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts: corporate income tax (RC), GST/HST (RT) where taxable supplies exceed the $30,000 registration threshold, and payroll (RP) if employees are hired in Canada. Use the Certificate of Incorporation and the CRA business activity code for software publishing (NAICS 511210) to complete registration. A corporate bank account should be opened after the corporation possesses its BN and certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Initial director/officer identification and residential history
Registered office address and mailing address
Estimated revenue, payroll, and business activity description for CRA questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, respond to the account verification request with the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office confirmation, and a description of the mobile utility app business. If the business activity code is incorrect, amend the CRA program account via Business Registration Online or by written request; potential penalties are avoided by timely correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. ISIC 6201 software publishing and mobile utility application development do not constitute a prescribed physical or industrial manufacturing activity under Alberta law; no provincial industrial licensing board approval is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No manufacturing or industrial operating permit applies. The corporation distributes software through app stores and does not require an Alberta industrial operating licence. A municipal business licence may be required if a physical office is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) — not applicable for a virtual software-only business; applicable only if future physical premises, construction, or regulated environmental activities are undertaken.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no fixed industrial facility, point-source discharge, or atmospheric emission is associated with the mobile utility app operation. EIA registration or full EIA report is not triggered at incorporation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered. If the company later leases physical office or data-centre space, it must comply with municipal wastewater and solid waste bylaws, Alberta OHS electrical safety requirements, e-waste disposal standards, and any landlord environmental requirements. No VOC or wastewater process thresholds apply to software publishing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a remote-first software company with no physical premises. If the corporation leases office space, obtain a municipal occupancy permit, fire safety inspection, and structural/occupational clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code, including general fire prevention, emergency evacuation, and accessibility compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada); primary portal: CRA My Business Account, supplemented by the Government of Canada Business Registration Online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon federal or Alberta incorporation, the registrar transmits corporate details to CRA, which issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN). GST/HST account registration is made through Business Registration Online, My Business Account, or Form RC1; non-resident corporations use Form RC171 to obtain a BN and may apply for GST/HST registration if they carry on business in Canada. The applicant must provide the legal entity name, registered office, directors, ISIC/NAICS business classification, and, for non-residents, a Canadian representative or address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation is a resident taxpayer subject to Canadian federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax on worldwide income; Alberta income is attributed under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act through a permanent establishment. No pass-through eligibility and no tax-exempt zone classification applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box regime. Corpus of applicable elections includes: income tax rollover elections (ITA s. 85), capital dividend elections (ITA s. 83(2)), associated-company designation elections, GST/HST closely related corporation election (Excise Tax Act s. 156), GST/HST Quick Method election, annual GST/HST filing election, and non-resident election under ITA s. 216 for Canadian-source rental income. Hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and non-elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); in Alberta only the federal 5% GST applies because the province has no provincial PST/HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of total worldwide taxable supplies (before deductions) from Canadian commercial activity, determined in any calendar quarter or over the prior four consecutive calendar quarters; exceeding this gross turnover mandate requires GST/HST registration. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada are subject to the same small-supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no government real-time fiscal clearance, continuous controls, or digital stamping mandate. GST/HST registrants must issue valid tax invoices containing the registrant's name, BN, invoice date, description of supply and tax amount. Large registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5 million must file GST/HST returns electronically. CRA requires books and records to be retained in machine-readable format where generated electronically; e-invoicing is accepted but not cleared by CRA in real time.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Canada, and services or intangible personal property supplied to non-resident recipients, may be zero-rated for GST/HST where the supply qualifies under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act. For a mobile utility application sold through Apple App Store or Google Play, digitally delivered software supplied to non-residents who use and receive the app outside Canada is generally zero-rated; the supplier must evidence the non-resident status of the recipient, the foreign download/store account, foreign IP or device metadata, and absence of use or supply in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or equivalent electronic export declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (where physical media or goods are exported)
Contract, order, purchase records, and downloaded-app transactional records
Payment settlement evidence and foreign currency inward remittance certificate or bank confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated export claims within the normal four-year assessment window, extended to ten years in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful omission. Failure to retain the required documentary substantiation can result in denial of zero-rating, reassessment of GST/HST at the applicable rate, interest, and penalties under the Excise Tax Act. Gross negligence penalties may reach 50% of the tax understated or the overstatement of refund; deliberate falsification of export or non-residency evidence may attract criminal prosecution and retrospective clawback of refunded GST/HST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Foreign exchange administration is not centralised in a single control authority comparable to other jurisdictions; relevant mandates are distributed among the Bank of Canada (monetary authority and Retail Payment Activities Act registration authority), Department of Finance Canada (policy), Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC, AML/CFT), and Statistics Canada (balance-of-payments and International Transactions Reporting System).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current account convertibility under a free-floating exchange rate regime. The Canadian dollar is a freely tradeable currency with no exchange-control legislation restricting conversion of CAD, acquisition of foreign currency, or repatriation of capital, dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees. Profit remittance is not subject to pre-clearance or central bank approval; however, outbound payments to non-residents may attract Part XIII withholding tax (generally 25% under the Income Tax Act, reduced to 5-15% under applicable tax treaties, including the Canada-US Treaty). No minimum duration for capital to remain in Canada and no forced conversion at prescribed rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline applies to export receipts or foreign-currency earnings. Canadian exporters and service providers may retain proceeds in foreign-currency accounts at Schedule I or II banks, may freely convert to CAD, and are not required to report routine receipts to the Bank of Canada. Only statistical reporting to Statistics Canada under the International Transactions Reporting System (threshold commonly CAD 1,000,000 for direct investment flows) may apply, and that is data reporting rather than an exchange-control permit requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD) with Capital Escrow sub-account
Operational Account (CAD/USD); Capital Escrow Account available across Alberta branches
Operational Account; Global Transaction Banking trade settlement rails and USD clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium as a standalone treasury rail. Canada does not recognise the EU/UK-style Electronic Money Institution licence with passporting rights. A non-resident EMI must either register under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) directly with the Bank of Canada if it provides payment functions in Canada, or operate through an authorised Canadian payment service provider. The RPAA registration is activity-based and requires a Canadian establishment for full compliance with safeguarding, operational risk, and segregation obligations. A foreign EMI can therefore supplement, but not replace, a Schedule I bank account; using an offshore EMI for core treasury flows creates FINTRAC reporting complexity, sub-outsourcing risk, and FX inefficiency. Recommended hierarchy: Schedule I bank as anchor, licensed Canadian PSP (e.g., fintech subsidiaries of the Big Six banks) for alternative acquirer flows, and offshore EMI only for niche SaaS vendor payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under FINTRAC's PCMLTFA identification rules using video-conference, digital identity verification, or credit-file-based methods; nevertheless, most Canadian Schedule I banks still require at least one director or authorised signatory to complete a live video KYC interview, and physical in-branch attendance is frequently mandated for the first account opening where the corporation is newly incorporated, non-resident directors exist, or beneficial ownership is layered. For an Alberta business corporation with a Canadian director, a hybrid path (video call plus one in-person branch visit by the Canadian resident director) will materially accelerate onboarding and eliminate most discretionary bank risk appetite rejections. Fully remote opening without any Canadian nexus is uncommon and may be declined for capital escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain opacity where shareholders comprise intermediate holding companies in multiple foreign jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry certified Certificate of Status; CBCA or ABCA Register of Individuals with Significant Control; consolidated ownership chart tracing through each intermediate entity to ultimate natural persons; foreign registry abstracts for each holding company; notarised passports of all UBOs; written confirmation that no nominee shareholding exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection source-of-funds unverified from non-resident shareholders funding a newly incorporated Alberta company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; 90-day bank statements of each subscribing shareholder; source-of-wealth declaration; signed audited or reviewed parent financial statements; good-standing certificate from the shareholder's home corporate registry; notarised board resolution authorising the capital contribution; detailed narrative of the commercial rationale for the Canadian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed persons (PEP), or adverse-media screening alerts on directors, shareholders, or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alert-specific explanatory memorandum; official identification documents and proof of residential address; independent legal opinion confirming the individual is not a designated person under Canadian sanctions; sworn affidavit where the alert arises from name-alias coincidence; enhanced due diligence questionnaire; evidence of prior banking relationship with a regulated institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No substantive physical operating address or mismatch between registered office and actual Alberta business premises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Alberta office lease or sublease; utility bill dated within 60 days; corporate-registration agent acknowledgement distinguishing registered office from operating address; photographic or video walkthrough of premises if requested; payroll or equipment lease evidence demonstrating active local operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected transaction flows inconsistent with stated business, notably recurring app-store micro-receipts (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing) versus large intermittent treasury wires for equity injections or intercompany settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with revenue projections for the mobile utility software application; App Store Connect and Google Play Console developer contracts evidencing merchant-of-record and net payout mechanics; pro forma cash-flow forecast covering 12 months; executed intercompany services and treasury support agreements; historical payout statements from Apple and Google; banking questionnaire outlining expected monthly transaction frequency and value ranges.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or, for bank-to-bank reimbursements, MT202, credited to the CAD or USD operational or capital escrow account at the Alberta branch of the sponsoring Schedule I bank. Payment narratives should carry the classifying 'reason for payment' indicating Direct Investment - Equity Capital, and the bank will apply the Canadian Balance of Payments taxonomy for Statistics Canada ITRS reporting of transactions at or above CAD 1,000,000; no Bank of Canada pre-approval or permit is required. For electronic funds transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000, FINTRAC reporting obligations arise, and the wire must contain structured originator and beneficiary KYC fields (name, address, account number and, where required, identification reference) compliant with Payment Canada and Wolfsberg standards. App-store operating inflows from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing arrive separately as merchant-of-record net settlements (typically USD via Apple Canada Inc. or Google entities), and should be directed to the designated USD operating account with a standing instruction to sweep balances into CAD through the bank's automated conversion facility.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and intercompany disbursements should use: (i) SWIFT MT103 single-credit message for SaaS licensing fees, SDK provider charges, marketing payments, and intercompany settlements below letter-of-credit thresholds; (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT707 irrevocable commercial letters of credit, confirmed where counterparty or country risk necessitates, for material technology licensing milestones or lump-sum IP acquisition disbursements; and (iii) Lynx (Payments Canada high-value payment system, ISO 20022-native) for same-day CAD-denominated transfers within Canada, including zero-balance sweeping across CAD and USD umbrella accounts. Multi-currency payables are settled via the bank's foreign exchange desk with same-day conversion against mid-market rates, spread governance under treasury policy, and standing custody of ISDA or Canadian Master FX documentation. For recurring app-store commission payments to Apple and Google, no wire instructions are required as deductions occur at source in the merchant-of-record settlement cycle.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forwards (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, tenors up to 24 months)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to cross-currency exposures involving inconvertible emerging-market currencies where a subsidiary or supplier invoices in a restricted currency; CAD itself is freely deliverable and does not require NDF treatment
Foreign exchange swaps (simultaneous spot and forward legs with the same counterparty for liquidity and tenor management)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (ISDA-documented, subject to bank credit and derivatives suitability review)
European-style OTC FX options (put and call structures) for risk-reversal or premium-budget hedging of forecast foreign-currency receipts from app-store payouts
Zero-cost collars and participating forwards where the treasury governance framework approves premium-neutral structures with defined strike corridors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and executed shareholder minutes/resolutions, including election of directors and auditor waiver (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records office of the corporation (not filed with a regulator; retained for CRA and lender inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM no later than 18 months after incorporation; thereafter no more than 15 months after the previous AGM (ABCA s.122). Officers should target within 6 months after fiscal year-end to support tax filings.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No regulator monetary penalty; however, failure to hold an AGM invalidates unanimous auditor-waiver resolutions, exposes directors to statutory liability, and may be raised by CRA in an audit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (AR) confirming registered office, directors and address; a pre-requisite for status certificate issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta (Alberta Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the incorporation date (ABCA s.101); no extension is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late-filing monetary penalty in Alberta; however, default on annual returns for two consecutive years triggers a Registrar's notice and, after 120 days unremedied, administrative dissolution (ABCA ss.212-213). Revived by court or Registrar revival application (ABCA s.213).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (T2), including Alberta corporate income tax schedules, financial statements and shareholder details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Tax Services Office for the corporation's domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the taxation year-end (ITA s.150(1)); e.g., a December 31 year-end return is due June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months) under ITA s.162(2)-(3); arrears interest accrues at prescribed rates under ITA s.161; habitual non-filing may lead to deemed assessments, income estimates and enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and election renewal for annual filing (applicable when annual taxable supplies do not exceed CAD 1,500,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual GST/HST return due no later than 3 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); required instalments remain due quarterly.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file / failure-to-remit penalty of 5% of the net amount owing plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months) under Excise Tax Act s.280; prescribed-rate interest on arrears under ETA s.280.1.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporations Returns Act Annual Return (Form CR-1) — only when statutory thresholds are met (assets exceeding CAD 1,000,000, revenues exceeding CAD 10,000,000, or foreign-controlled status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Senior Statistics Officer, Corporations Returns Act, Statistics Canada (transmitted via CRA-coordinated process)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually by the pre-printed date on the Statistics Canada return, generally within 90 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Corporations Returns Act: summary conviction / indictable fines (up to CAD 20,000) and possible imprisonment for obstruction or false statements; Statistics Canada may also issue a formal demand for information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: ABCA Part 13 er demands an auditor for every distributing corporation (public-issuing). A private Business Corporation (non-distributing) may dispense with an external auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution; no revenue/asset dollar threshold alone triggers the audit, but shareholders representing at least 5% of issued voting shares may requisition a mandatory audit at an annual meeting (ABCA s.157). Lenders, investors or CRA may contractually or administratively require audited financial statements (e.g., for transfer-pricing, SR&ED, or unreported revenue reviews).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS (Part I) is mandatory for publicly accountable orchestras and reporting issuers; the private Alberta app company may adopt ASPE (Part II) or elect IFRS. ASPE is the presumptive framework for a private mobile-utility software company with entrusted/limited revenue from app-store billing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not currently impose an annual UBO filing for a private ABCA corporation: the statutory annual return captures only registered office and directors. For share transfers, directors' approval must be recorded and the Register of Members updated before the transferee exercises voting or dividend rights (ABCA ss.106-110); no Alberta registry transfer filing is required. An internal annual UBO attestation should identify all individuals owning 25% or more of the equity and/or exercising de facto control to be ready for the pending Alberta transparency regime (Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2024, not yet proclaimed) and in case the group adopts a federal CBCA vehicle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120–800 per year typical for registered office/registered agent services; full outsourced corporate secretarial maintenance (AGM, annual return, registers, UBO attestation) ranges from USD 1,000–3,500 per year in Alberta.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–12,000 for a certified audited financial statement of a small private mobile utility software corporation; USD 1,500–4,500 for a review engagement when audit is waived.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
